$comment: SUPERSEDED by the 2026 edition (mappings/owasp_llm_top10_2026.json) on 2026-08-17. Retained deliberately and DO NOT REGENERATE: dataset releases up to and including v2.9.0 (and their Zenodo DOIs) carry owasp_llm codes under THESE 2025 semantics, and cannot be read correctly without this table. The 2026 renumbering reuses the same code space LLM01-LLM10 with different meanings - see mappings/owasp_llm_2025_to_2026.json for the crosswalk.

LLM01.name: Prompt Injection
LLM01.description: A prompt injection vulnerability occurs when user prompts alter the LLM's behavior or output in unintended ways. Includes direct and indirect prompt injection.

LLM02.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
LLM02.description: LLMs may inadvertently disclose confidential data, proprietary algorithms, or other sensitive information through their output.

LLM03.name: Supply Chain
LLM03.description: LLM application lifecycle can be compromised by vulnerable components, services, or pre-trained models, leading to security breaches.

LLM04.name: Data and Model Poisoning
LLM04.description: Pre-training, fine-tuning, or embedding data is manipulated to introduce vulnerabilities, backdoors, or biases.

LLM05.name: Improper Output Handling
LLM05.description: Insufficient validation, sanitization, or handling of LLM-generated outputs before passing to downstream systems, enabling XSS, SQLi, SSRF, RCE, etc.

LLM06.name: Excessive Agency
LLM06.description: LLM-based systems granted excessive functionality, permissions, or autonomy that exceed what is required for the intended use.

LLM07.name: System Prompt Leakage
LLM07.description: Disclosure of system prompts that may contain instructions, sensitive context, or proprietary configuration.

LLM08.name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
LLM08.description: Weaknesses in how vectors and embeddings are generated, stored, or retrieved (RAG systems) — including embedding inversion and poisoning.

LLM09.name: Misinformation
LLM09.description: LLMs produce false or misleading information that appears credible, leading to security breaches, reputational damage, or legal liability.

LLM10.name: Unbounded Consumption
LLM10.description: LLM applications allow excessive or uncontrolled inferences, causing denial of service, financial losses, IP theft, or service degradation.
